correctness.rationale: For unordered two-token configurations the AA, AB and BB layers have degrees 2n, N-2 and 2m, respectively, and there are only AA–AB and BB–AB off-diagonal blocks. An AA pair couples to each AB pair containing one of its A vertices, giving the unsigned incidence block tensored with the all-ones vector on B, and symmetrically for BB. The incidence Gram matrix on an r-vertex part is (r-2)I+J, giving full rank for r>=3 and singular values sqrt(2r-2) on constants and sqrt(r-2) on the zero-sum subspace. The two outer incidence kernels give eigenvalues 2n and 2m in dimensions m(m-3)/2 and n(n-3)/2; the tensor product of the two zero-sum spaces in AB gives N-2 in dimension (m-1)(n-1). Coupling just the A-zero-sum directions to their AB lifts gives the two-by-two block with trace m+3n-2 and determinant n(m+2n-2), and hence roots n and m+2n-2, each repeated m-1 times. The B-zero-sum block gives m and n+2m-2, each repeated n-1 times. In the remaining three-layer constant block, the off-diagonal magnitudes are sqrt(2n(m-1)) and sqrt(2m(n-1)). Its determinant is zero from the constant token vector, its trace is 3N-2, and its order-two principal minors sum to 2N(N-1); its roots are 0,N,2N-2. These orthogonal pieces exhaust binom(N,2) dimensions. Vanishing kernel dimensions at a side length of three and coincident numerical eigenvalues are handled by the stated multiplicity convention. There is exactly one zero, so the graph is connected; multiplying the positive eigenvalues and dividing by binom(N,2) leaves 4 from the two exceptional nonzero constant-layer roots, as asserted. The bundled numerical and modular checker was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the infinite claim.

evidence: The exclusion Hamiltonian on the biclique is mn/2 - 2 S_1 dot S_2, with eigenvalues mn/2 + S_1(S_1+1) + S_2(S_2+1) - S(S+1) under spin coupling. The local multiplicity of spin r/2-a on r sites is binom(r,a)-binom(r,a-1).
The complement/Johnson theorem gives general simultaneous spectral pairing; the gap and cograph integrality theorems cover weaker consequences.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Use the full local spin decompositions in the Hamiltonian, not only the locally symmetric spin subspace. The spin-pair decomposition and fixed weight recover the required eigenspaces for two particles as a special case of the operator on the full occupation space. The complement theorem is another route: the complement token graph has components J(m,2), K_m square K_n, and J(n,2); the one-token lifts identify which complement eigenvalues belong to the 0 and N Johnson sectors, and the rest pair with 2N-2.

evidence: Set a=m/2-S_1, b=n/2-S_2, c=N/2-S. For two particles M=2-N/2, so c is 0, 1 or 2 with a+b<=c; impose nonnegative allowed local spins and the usual spin triangle range. Each admissible total spin contributes one state at this fixed M for each of the local spin copies.

The eigenvalue becomes c(N+1-c)-a(m+1-a)-b(n+1-b), of multiplicity [binom(m,a)-binom(m,a-1)][binom(n,b)-binom(n,b-1)]. For (a,b)=(0,0), c=0,1,2 gives 0,N,2N-2. For (1,0) and (0,1), c=1,2 gives n and m+2n-2, or m and n+2m-2, respectively. At c=2, (1,1), (2,0), (0,2) give N-2,2n,2m with the asserted dimensions; the nonexistent local spin at a side size of three corresponds to multiplicity zero.
